passage:
"Show me the report card."
"Amma..."
"Ojas."
He handed it over. Trisha read it in silence, her mouth thinning at the maths line. "I expected better," she said finally.
"I know. I feel like I've let you down."
"Did you study?"
"Not enough. I skipped the practice papers. That's on me. I nearly hid it from you."
"Why didn't you?"
"Because that would be worse."
Trisha sighed and sat down. "A mark is a mark. It isn't the whole of you. What do you need to do better?"
"Help with algebra. Could I go to Sir's extra class?"
"Yes. Ask him tomorrow." She put her hand on the card. "We'll fix this together."

qa.q: Which line of the report card made Trisha's mouth thin?
How does Ojas feel about his result, and what does he admit about it?
qa.a: He feels he has let his mother down. He admits he didn't study enough and skipped practice papers, and that he nearly hid the card.

qa.q: What did Ojas do that was helpful after the disappointing result?
qa.a: He owned the result, didn't hide the card, and asked for help by requesting the extra algebra class. 🙂

qa.q: How might Trisha be feeling as she talks with Ojas?
qa.a: Disappointed by the mark but still supportive. She says a mark is not the whole of him and offers to fix it together.

grounding: A parent is disappointed by the protagonist's result; he owns it, asks for help and does not hide the report card.

passage:
Gautam's father ran the fertiliser shop on the main road of Sehore, and every customer knew Gautam was supposed to top Class 10. When the half-yearly results came, he had come ninth.

"Just keep the card in your bag," his cousin Abhinav said on the bus home. "Tell Chacha the school is sending it next week. By then the finals will fix it."

Gautam watched the fields go by. His throat felt thick. Hiding it would buy a week. It would also mean lying every evening at the shop.

He got off at the stop and walked straight into the shop, past the sacks. "Papa, my result." His father read it standing at the counter, slowly.

"Ninth." Papa let out a long breath. "I expected more."

"Me too, Papa. I didn't understand accounts at all. Can Sharma Sir's evening class take me?"

Papa was silent, then said, "Ninth is not the end. We'll ask him tomorrow."

qa.q: Where did Gautam's father run his shop?
qa.a: Gautam's father ran the fertiliser shop on the main road of Sehore.

qa.q: How can you tell Gautam felt anxious on the bus?
qa.a: His throat felt thick as he stared at the fields, showing how afraid he was of disappointing his father.

qa.q: What went right when Gautam reached the shop?
qa.a: He showed the card straight away, owned the result and asked for help with accounts, instead of hiding it as Abhinav suggested.

qa.q: Why might Abhinav have suggested hiding the card?
qa.a: Abhinav probably wanted to protect Gautam from his father's disappointment, without thinking about the week of lying it would take.

grounding: It shows a teen whose parent is disappointed by his result, choosing to own it and ask for help rather than hide the report card.
